blocks.text: You can perform the following actions on a Decoy Connector:

blocks.item: Obtain Decoy Connector Recovery and Diagnostics Credentials

After you add and connect a Decoy Connector to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal, its recovery and diagnostic passwords are randomized. You can obtain the new credentials from the Deception Admin Portal.
Only users with the super admin role can view recovery credentials. To learn more, see About Users & Roles.
To obtain the recovery and diagnostics credentials:
Go to Settings > Topology > Decoy Connectors.
Locate the required Decoy Connector, and then click Actions > Credentials.
See image.
Copy the required credentials, and click Close.
See image.
Reboot a Decoy Connector
You can reboot a configured Decoy Connector in the Deception Admin Portal.
To reboot a Decoy Connector:
Go to Settings > Topology > Decoy Connectors.
Locate the required Decoy Connector, and then click Actions > Reboot.
See image.
In the confirmation window, click OK.
View Decoy Connector Update Logs
You can use the update logs to troubleshoot issues related to Decoy Connector updates.
To view the update logs:
Go to Settings > Topology > Decoy Connectors.
Locate the required Decoy Connector, and then click Logs > View update logs.
See image.
View the logs as necessary, and then click Close.
See image.
Download Decoy Connector Debug Logs

Debug logs are system-generated logs that are stored on a Decoy Connector. Debug logs are copied to the Deception Admin Portal when you initiate a download request. The logs contain timestamps and messages that help you troubleshoot any issues with network decoys or other integrations that use Decoy Connectors.
For a Decoy Connector, you can download either the most recent or all debug logs.
Make sure that the Decoy Connector is connected to the Deception Admin Portal before you download the debug logs.
To download debug logs:
Go to Settings > Topology > Decoy Connectors.
Locate the required Decoy Connector, and then click Logs.
Select an option from the Logs drop-down menu:
Request recent debug logs: Download the last 1,000 lines from each log file.
Request all debug logs: Download the complete log files.
See image.
After the request is initiated and completed, click Download debug logs.
In the Debug Logs window, click the Download icon.
See image.
The debug logs are downloaded as a .tar.xz file. Extract the file using a file compression tool (e.g., WinZip, 7-zip, etc.).
If the debug log files consume a large amount of disk space, you can periodically delete them. Click the Delete icon to delete the logs from the Deception Admin Portal.
See image.
Click Close.
Edit or Delete a Decoy Connector
You can edit or delete a configured Decoy Connector in the Deception Admin Portal.
Deception uses Private Access (ZPA) or Threat Intelligence Decoy Connectors to deploy decoys in a dedicated Deception cloud. You cannot edit or delete them. Contact Zscaler Support to manage them.
To edit a Decoy Connector:
Go to Settings > Topology > Decoy Connectors.
Locate the required Decoy Connector, and then click Actions > Edit.
See image.
In the Decoy Connector Details window, modify the required values.
See image.
Click Save.
To delete a Decoy Connector:
Go to Settings > Topology > Decoy Connectors.
Locate the required Decoy Connector, and then click Actions > Delete.
See image.
In the confirmation window, click OK.
